title: Introduce per-lane batch arenas and slipstream scheduler to reduce KV GC and tail latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Over the last two quarters we've observed repeated GC spikes and heap fragmentation originating from the shared KV cache metadata and the global continuous-batcher state. These spikes correlate with tail-latency outliers on long-lived streams and during bursty arrival patterns. While prior work added heuristics to warm and prefetch keys, the root cause remains contention and working-set churn in a globally shared heap and a monolithic batch state machine.

Proposal: Re-anchor the continuous-batcher runtime by (1) introducing per-lane memory arenas for ephemeral batch/session state and compact KV metadata slabs, and (2) replacing the global scheduler runloop with a "slipstream" scheduler: a work-stealing-friendly, low-lock runloop that minimizes synchronous cross-lane traversal during admission and draining. The combination should reduce GC pressure, cut allocation churn, and shrink tail latencies during bursts.

Scope and non-goals: Scope covers runtime components inside the serving process: batch state, slot lifecycles, and the in-memory KV cache index footprint. Non-goals include persistent on-disk format changes, network admission protocols, or Dedicated control-plane orchestration. This is a low-risk refactor—no model semantics changes.

Design summary:
- Per-lane arenas: allocate batch-scoped objects (session descriptors, token windows, temporary buffers) from small per-lane arenas that can be bulk-reset on lane quiesce. Move KV cache transient metadata (session pointers, last-access stamps used for warmup heuristics) into compact slab structures with predictable layout and manual free lists.
- Slipstream scheduler: implement a lightweight per-lane runloop that accepts local enqueues and exposes a short, bounded steal window for neighboring lanes. Admission logic moves from synchronous global locks to optimistic handoffs, falling back to a single atomic steal when contention is detected.
- Upgrade path: introduce the arenas behind a feature flag so we can A/B traffic and perform canary rollouts. Provide compatibility layer so older snapshots can be interpreted.

Migration plan:
1) Prototype arena allocator and slab-backed KV-index in a feature branch and run microbenchmarks (allocation rate, pause times) and stress tests with replayed production traces.
2) Implement slipstream scheduler and validate fairness with synthetic adversarial arrivals.
3) Canary deploy to a non-critical shard of Dedicated for 48–72 hours under production-like load.
4) Gradual rollout with telemetry dashboards and automatic rollback if tail latency or errors regress beyond thresholds.

Risks and mitigations:
- Memory leaks from manual arenas: mitigate with unit tests, address sanitizer builds, and leak detectors in canary.
- Scheduling regressions causing head-of-line blocking: mitigate with a short steal window and conservative fallbacks to current scheduler under high error rate.
- Hard-to-debug crashes from allocator changes: ship with feature flag and a fast rollback path; add detailed heap diagnostics when enabled.

Deliverables:
- Feature-flagged arena allocator and slab-backed KV-index implementation.
- Slipstream scheduler implementation with metrics and tracing hooks.
- Microbenchmarks, stress test harness, and replay job for production traces.
- Dashboards for allocation rate, GC pause distribution, lane imbalance, steal rate, and tail latency.
- Design doc, migration runbook, and postmortem template for canary failures.
acceptance_criteria: Canary traffic shows >=25% reduction in 95th/99th percentile GC pause duration compared to baseline for the same workload
End-to-end 99th-percentile token latency improves by at least 10% under bursty arrival traces used in replay tests
No increase in error rate or dropped sessions in canary; any regressions must be explainable and <=0.1% relative
Feature is toggleable at process start and can be rolled back without data loss
Comprehensive tracing and allocation metrics added and visible in runtime-2.3 dashboard
comments: 2026-02-05 - Aisha Patel: Spiked initial prototype of per-lane arena. Microbenchmarks show 40% fewer malloc calls at steady state. Allocator API sketched in design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RT/pages/arena-design-v1

2026-02-12 - Marcus Zhu: Implemented slab-backed KV-index prototype in branch eng/ENG-890123/kv-slab. Running replay on ci/trace-run-2026-01. Observed 18% lower RSS but some increased fragmentation in long-lived sessions. Investigating free-list reuse patterns.

2026-02-20 - Design review notes: PM and SRE requested metric hooks for lane occupancy, steal attempts, and per-lane allocation rate. Added to spec. Action: add sentinel sampling when the arena-reset happens to ensure no dangling pointers.

2026-02-28 - QA: Stress harness hit an intermittent assertion in the slipstream steal path (race with lane shutdown). Temporary mitigation: extend grace period and add CAS-based shutdown marker. Fix planned in next PR.

2026-03-10 - Marcus Zhu: Open PR for slipstream runloop (GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3821). Benchmarked under rr-trace-04: 95th token latency down 12% vs baseline; GC pause tail down ~30% in run with 80% long-lived sessions.
2026-03-12 - Aisha Patel: Preparing canary runbook. Canary + observability checklist complete. Targeting non-customer critical Dedicated shard next week. Notifying support and oncall rotations.
